title: Gathering the Qur'an flow chart
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The Rightly Guided Caliphs: Abu Bakr and Umar
source: Written for islamic-studies/y6 lesson 18 (Pupil PDF worksheet: gathering the Qur'an flow chart)
intro: Lesson 18: Abu Bakr's leadership and the compilation of the Qur'an. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A firm leader
points: He sent Usamah's army as the Prophet ﷺ had planned
He stood firm when some refused zakah

panels.title: Why gather the Qur'an?
points: At Yamamah, many huffaz were killed
Umar feared parts could be lost
Abu Bakr agreed after thinking carefully

blocks.text: Boxes and arrows only: write one step in each box.

keywords.def: a written copy of the Qur'an
someone who has memorised the Qur'an
the scribe who gathered the Qur'an

questions.q: Explain why the Qur'an was gathered into one copy.
questions.a: Many memorisers were killed at Yamamah; gathering it in writing made sure none was lost.

questions.q: Draw a flow chart (boxes and arrows only) on the pupil PDF of how the Qur'an was gathered, then write in the portal response box why Zayd was a good choice. Start: 'Zayd was a good choice because ...'
questions.a: Correct steps; Zayd was young, trusted, a scribe of revelation and careful

questions.q: Extend: who kept the copy after Abu Bakr?

questions.a: Allah promised to protect the Qur'an; the gathering is one way He did it.

questions.q: Who gathered the Qur'an for Abu Bakr?
questions.a: A) Zayd ibn Thabit. Zayd ibn Thabit, a scribe of the revelation (Bukhari).
A written copy of the Qur'an
options: A written copy of the Qur'an

questions.q: Think again: how do you protect something precious kept in memory?
questions.a: Write it carefully and check it against memory.
